evidence.headline: One LAN run on these files
evidence.framing: Observed in one physical Windows-to-Android LAN run. Evidence, not a universal performance guarantee.
evidence.scope: Exact {{RELEASE_LABEL}} Windows host and Android APK
items: One video reassembly drop, recovered in 229 ms
Computer audio decoded with no reported underruns; audible output was not independently confirmed
Variable-cadence test source averaged 49.35 rendered fps
caveats: This does not validate sustained smooth 60 fps.
Six capture recreations caused presentation gaps over 200 ms, longest 285 ms.
Audible playback, a 30-minute endurance run, physical remote input, and unrelated-network media remain unqualified.

status_legend.meaning: In these files. The line says if a physical run is still missing.

capability_groups.title: Sending and watching
capability_groups.intro: In the public Windows and Android builds. If a physical run is still missing, the same line says so.

items.name: Screen and window capture
items.detail: Share an entire screen, or pick a single window, from a Windows x64 PC.

items.name: Video quality controls
items.detail: Choose 60 or 30 fps and adjust stream quality while a session is running. Those controls do not promise sustained 60 fps on every PC.

items.name: H.264 encoding
items.detail: NVIDIA NVENC is the validated path. Other PCs fall back to the built-in Windows CPU encoder, which costs processor time. Vendor hardware acceleration and physical Intel/AMD streaming tests are still pending.

items.name: Android receiving
items.detail: Android 8 or newer, decoding in hardware. Validated on one device in the public {{RELEASE_LABEL}} run.

items.name: Windows receiving
items.detail: A second Windows PC can receive the screen and system audio. Both ends need matching builds.

items.name: Computer audio
items.detail: The sending PC’s audio travels with the screen. The receiver decoded computer audio in the LAN run with no reported underruns. Audible output on a phone was not independently confirmed.

capability_groups.title: Ships. Unproven.
capability_groups.intro: The control is in the UI. Nobody has signed off a physical test. That is Preview, not Available.

items.name: Private session admission
items.detail: The viewing device issues a private invitation that authorises the session over a pinned QUIC connection. Expiry, replay, and revocation pass loopback tests; physical regression testing is still open.

items.name: Two-way microphone voice
items.detail: Builds and passes its checks. Physical round-trip and echo testing have not been done.

items.name: Remote control from Android
items.detail: Builds and passes its checks. Physical input, and behaviour inside native games, are unproven.

items.name: Cursor appearance and effects
items.detail: Desktop cursor styling with a local effects budget. The current build labels this preview only.

capability_groups.title: Needs something you already run
capability_groups.intro: We do not sell you a cloud for this. Off-LAN viewing needs a route you already have. Contacts stay on the PC.

items.name: Viewing outside your local network
items.detail: Works across a private mesh you already run. STUN probing is implemented; automatic universal Internet traversal is not. A reachable route has to exist first.

items.name: Device-owned accounts and contacts
items.detail: Held locally on Windows. Sync, recovery, and global handle claims are not implemented.

capability_groups.title: Not in this download
capability_groups.intro: Do not look for these in {{RELEASE_LABEL}}.

items.name: Automatic update checks
items.detail: Present in some development builds, not in this download. Update by installing a newer matching Windows and Android pair over the old one.

items.name: Managed relay and multi-viewer rooms
items.detail: There is no FastCast-run media relay, and multi-viewer rooms are not implemented.

items.name: macOS, Linux, iPhone, and iPad
items.detail: Not implemented. This preview is Windows x64 and Android 8 or newer only. Android does not send.

limitations: Windows binaries are unsigned; Android is debug-signed.
A reachable peer route such as a LAN or private mesh is required.
Automatic universal Internet traversal is not available.
A FastCast-managed media relay is not available.
Android is a viewer in this public release, not a sender.
macOS, Linux, iPhone, iPad, and browser apps are not available.
